title: Why I don't do many (if any) let's play videos (and who to watch instead)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ANYrzwn5h_M

Daniel (@dungeondive) steps out from behind the games for a channel-update vlog, answering a recurring request: why won't he do playthrough videos? The honest answer, five years and many reviews later, is that he hates making them. He offers three reasons. First, he's slightly dyslexic with a poor memory, which makes him a shaky rules player, and filming a playthrough just memorialises every mistake for commenters to catalogue — no fun. Second, he doesn't even enjoy watching long board-game let's-plays; as a viewer he wants a game's vibe, its look on the table, and an honest opinion, not an unedited rules slog. Third, his actual play style — "slow questing," a few turns here, more the next day — is hostile to filming: shifting light, bumped tables, broken continuity. He argues the polished, voice-booth-and-drone-shot solo-RPG playthroughs now proliferating set unrealistic expectations, and points viewers toward channels he trusts for the format instead — the Solo Gamers Club above all, plus Mage Hammer's Game Table, Stone Axe Game Table, Cat Weasel, and Kalosmar. It's a clarifying statement of what the Dungeon Dive is for, and — landing years after the aborted City of Kings experiment — reads as the retrospective epitaph for exactly that kind of video.

----

Daniel makes the case that unedited let's-plays aren't what he wants to make or watch. As a viewer, what do you actually want from a board-game channel — the full play experience, or the vibe, the look, and an honest opinion?
